## Claims
- [proved] In the bounded \(a=1,b=2\) box/Pieri setting defined below, the Schur columns and all generators of the Pieri-row lattice are complete in degrees \(d+1\) and \(d+2\).
- [proved] For \(p=c=1\), the degree-\(d+2\) row matrix, with rows \((2),(3),(4)\) and columns \((x_2,z,y_2)\), is
  \[
  \begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}.
  \]
  Its rows \((2),(3)\) on columns \((z,y_2)\) form
  \[
  \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det=-1.
  \]

## Strategy
Put \(q=i+p,\ r=j+c,\ d=ij\), where
\[
i,j\ge2,\qquad p,c\ge1,\qquad \min(p,c)=1.
\]
Let \(R=i^j\), work in the \(q\times r\) Schur box, and let \(J\) have Schur basis indexed by partitions containing \(R\). Write
\[
Q=J/A_+J,\qquad A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q).
\]

Define
\[
x_0=s_R,\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},
\]
and
\[
u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})},\quad
x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})},\quad
z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)},
\]
\[
y_2=s_{(i^j,2)},\qquad
w=s_{(i^j,1,1)}.
\]
Here \(u\) exists exactly when \(p\ge2\), and \(w\) exists exactly when \(c\ge2\). The columns \(x_1,y_1,x_2,z,y_2\) always exist.

Every partition containing \(R\) with size \(d+1\) is exactly one of
\[
(i+1,i^{j-1}),\qquad(i^j,1),
\]
so \((x_1,y_1)\) is the complete degree-\(d+1\) column list. Pieri gives the sole row
\[
(1):\qquad h_1x_0=x_1+y_1.
\]
This is complete since \(J_d=\mathbb Zx_0\) and \(A_1=\mathbb Zh_1\). Its matrix is \((1\ 1)\), with unit pivot \(1\) on \(y_1\).

Every partition containing \(R\) with size \(d+2\) is among
\[
u,\ x_2,\ z,\ y_2,\ w.
\]
The box conditions above delete precisely \(u\) when \(p=1\), and precisely \(w\) when \(c=1\). Thus the displayed list is complete in every boundary case.

Since \(A_2=\mathbb Zh_2+\mathbb Zh_1^2\), and
\[
h_1^2x_0=h_1(h_1x_0)\in h_1J_{d+1},
\]
the complete degree-\(d+2\) relation lattice is generated by
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(2):&h_2x_0=u+z+y_2,\\
(3):&h_1x_1=u+x_2+z,\\
(4):&h_1y_1=z+y_2+w,
\end{array}
\]
with nonexistent boundary terms omitted.

There are three boundary cases.

1. If \(p=c=1\), columns are \((x_2,z,y_2)\), and the matrix is
   \[
   \begin{pmatrix}
   0&1&1\\
   1&1&0\\
   0&1&1
   \end{pmatrix}.
   \]
   Rows \((2),(3)\) on \((z,y_2)\) have determinant \(-1\). Rows \((2)\) and \((4)\) are equal.

2. If \(p=1,\ c\ge2\), columns are \((x_2,z,y_2,w)\), and the matrix is
   \[
   \begin{pmatrix}
   0&1&1&0\\
   1&1&0&0\\
   0&1&1&1
   \end{pmatrix}.
   \]
   On complementary columns \((z,y_2,w)\), its determinant is \(-1\).

3. If \(p\ge2,\ c=1\), columns are \((u,x_2,z,y_2)\), and the matrix is
   \[
   \begin{pmatrix}
   1&0&1&1\\
   1&1&1&0\\
   0&0&1&1
   \end{pmatrix}.
   \]
   On complementary columns \((u,z,y_2)\), its determinant is \(1\).

Thus in every case the stated rows are an integral, complete presentation of the degree-\(d+2\) relations, with a unimodular complementary minor. In particular, no omitted degree-\(d+1\) or degree-\(d+2\) Schur column or Pieri row remains.

## Gaps
- This certificate uses the stipulated box-Schur/Pieri presentation \(Q=J/A_+J\) and \(A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q)\). It does not establish that presentation or any global minimality statement.

## Next
The named completeness certificate in degrees \(d+1\) and \(d+2\) is established, conditional on the stated box/Pieri presentation.
